cards.text: Friend, meet Hezekiah, king of Judah. The LORD has saved him and Jerusalem from the king of Assyria, and now all the nations look up to him. Then, in those days, Hezekiah becomes mortally ill.

cards.question: Hezekiah, king of Judah, is mortally ill. What does he do?
When Hezekiah prays, the LORD speaks to him and gives him a sign.

cards.text: The LORD has shown Hezekiah favor, and when somebody does you a favor like THAT, you bake them a WHOLE box of thank-you cookies. Hezekiah? He doesn't repay the favor shown to him.

cards.question: Hezekiah doesn't repay the favor the LORD showed him. Why not?

answers.text: His advisers talk him out of it

cards.question: Because Hezekiah's heart is proud, wrath comes upon him and upon Judah and ___.

cards.text: Wrath on the king AND the whole country. Now Hezekiah has a choice to make about that pride.

cards.question: With wrath on him and his people, Hezekiah ___ the pride of his heart.
Hezekiah humbles himself all alone, while the people of Jerusalem stay proud.
Because Hezekiah and the people humble themselves, the wrath of the LORD doesn't come upon them during the days of ___.

cards.text: Friend, I KNOW pride. My first day in that junk drawer, I told the rubber bands I was way too good to be in there... and I said it lying UNDER a takeout menu.

Hezekiah has very great riches and honor: treasuries of silver, gold and precious stones, storehouses for grain, new wine and oil, herds and flocks in abundance, even cities, because God gave him very great wealth. Meanwhile I owned ONE handle with my name carved in it, and I thought I was LIVING.
Hezekiah's a builder too. At the Spring of Gihon, he blocks the upper outlet and sends that water somewhere new.

cards.question: Hezekiah blocks the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon. Where does he channel the water?

answers.text: Down to the west side of the City of David
Out east toward the Jordan River
South into the Valley of Hinnom

cards.text: Hezekiah prospers in all he does. Then visitors show up: ambassadors sent by the rulers of Babylon.

cards.question: Ambassadors from the rulers of Babylon come to Hezekiah. What do they want to ask about?

answers.text: The wonder that happened in the land

cards.question: While the ambassadors from Babylon are there, God leaves Hezekiah alone. Why?

answers.text: To test him and know all in his heart
To let him rest from his battles
To give the ambassadors room to talk

cards.text: The rest of Hezekiah's acts and his deeds of loving devotion are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. MY life story got written on the back of a takeout menu with a stubby pencil... and honestly? Still a page-turner.

cards.question: Hezekiah rests with his fathers. Where is he buried?

answers.text: In the upper tombs of David's descendants
In the garden of his own palace
In the cave of Machpelah at Hebron

cards.question: At Hezekiah's death, all Judah and the people of Jerusalem pay him honor.
After Hezekiah dies, his son ___ reigns in his place.

findings.problem: This story card runs to three sentences: the favor and cookie-box line, then "Hezekiah?", then "He doesn't repay the favor shown to him." That is more than the 1 to 2 sentences allowed for a story card after the opening.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card adds nothing new from the passage. "Wrath on the king AND the whole country" restates verse 25, which card 6 already asked about. The rest only sets up the next question. It works as a recap card and doesn't move the passage forward.
This story card tells no part of the passage. It is only a joke about the junk drawer, yet it cites 2 Chronicles 32:26, which it doesn't retell.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer episode: on his first day, Papa Dorin boasted to the rubber bands that he was too good to be there. That adds to his backstory, and it contradicts it. The backstory says he gave up on himself in the drawer and "didn't talk much. He didn't joke at all." Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Verses 27 to 29 are a long stretch: a list of Hezekiah's wealth, treasuries, storehouses, herds and cities. The summary card goes through it item by item (silver, gold, precious stones, grain, new wine, oil, herds, flocks, cities) instead of saying in a few words what it covers.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Down to the west side of the City of David", is noticeably longer and more specific than the two wrong answers, so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: This story card runs to three sentences: the verse 32 sentence, then the takeout-menu sentence ending "and honestly?", then "Still a page-turner." That is more than the 1 to 2 sentences allowed.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "MY life story got written on the back of a takeout menu" changes the backstory. He wrote a goodbye note to his drawer friends on the back of a menu, not his life story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
